sanskrit: tīkṣṇāṅkuśaśataghnībhir yantrajālaiś ca śobhitam āyasaiś ca mahācakraiḥ śuśubhe tat purottamam
english: Adorned with sharp elephant-goads, śataghni machines, and a network of war-engines, and further with great iron wheels, that finest of cities shone resplendent.

sanskrit: suvibhaktamahārathyaṃ devatābādhavarjitam virocamānaṃ vividhaiḥ pāṇḍurair bhavanottamaiḥ
english: With its broad avenues well laid out, free from the affliction of evil spirits, and brilliant with various magnificent white mansions, it blazed forth in glory.

sanskrit: tat triviṣṭapasaṃkāśam indraprasthaṃ vyarocata meghavṛndam ivākāśe vṛddhaṃ vidyutsamāvṛtam
english: That Indraprastha shone like the heaven of the gods, even as a great mass of clouds in the sky swells and is encircled with lightning.

sanskrit: tatra ramye śubhe deśe kauravyasya niveśanam śuśubhe dhanasaṃpūrṇaṃ dhanādhyakṣakṣayopamam
english: There, in that delightful and auspicious place, the dwelling of the Kauravya prince shone, filled with wealth, resembling the abode of Kubera, the lord of riches.

sanskrit: tatrāgacchan dvijā rājan sarvavedavidāṃ varāḥ nivāsaṃ rocayanti sma sarvabhāṣāvidas tathā
english: There, O king, came brahmins who were the foremost among all knowers of the Vedas, and they were pleased to take up residence there — men who were also versed in all languages.

sanskrit: vaṇijaś cābhyayus tatra deśe digbhyo dhanārthinaḥ sarvaśilpavidaś caiva vāsāyābhyāgamaṃs tadā
english: Merchants too came there from all directions seeking wealth, and all manner of artisans came to settle in that land at that time.

sanskrit: udyānāni ca ramyāṇi nagarasya samantataḥ āmrair āmrātakair nīpair aśokaiś campakais tathā
english: And charming gardens spread all around the city, with mango trees, hog-plum trees, kadamba trees, aśoka trees, and campaka trees —

sanskrit: puṃnāgair nāgapuṣpaiś ca lakucaiḥ panasais tathā śālatālakadambaiś ca bakulaiś ca saketakaiḥ
english: — with puṃnāga and nāgapuṣpa trees, lakuca and jackfruit trees, śāla, tāla and kadamba trees, bakula and saketaka trees,

sanskrit: manoharaiḥ puṣpitaiś ca phalabhārāvanāmitaiḥ prācīnāmalakair lodhrair aṅkolaiś ca supuṣpitaiḥ
english: — with lovely flowering trees bowed down under the weight of their fruits, with old āmalaka trees, lodhra trees, and aṅkola trees in full bloom,

sanskrit: jambūbhiḥ pāṭalābhiś ca kubjakair atimuktakaiḥ karavīraiḥ pārijātair anyaiś ca vividhair drumaiḥ
english: — with rose-apple trees, pāṭalā trees, kubjaka and atimuktaka creepers, karavīra and pārijāta trees, and many other trees of diverse kinds —

sanskrit: nityapuṣpaphalopetair nānādvijagaṇāyutam mattabarhiṇasaṃghuṣṭaṃ kokilaiś ca sadāmadaiḥ
english: — always bearing flowers and fruits, filled with flocks of birds of many species, resounding with the cries of intoxicated peacocks and ever-joyful cuckoos.

sanskrit: gṛhair ādarśavimalair vividhaiś ca latāgṛhaiḥ manoharaiś citragṛhais tathā jagatiparvataiḥ vāpībhir vividhābhiś ca pūrṇābhiḥ paramāmbhasā
english: The gardens were adorned with houses as pure and clear as mirrors, with various arbours of climbing plants, with charming painted pavilions and raised terraces like little hills, and with various step-wells brimming with the finest water.

sanskrit: sarobhir atiramyaiś ca padmotpalasugandhibhiḥ haṃsakāraṇḍavayutaiś cakravākopaśobhitaiḥ
english: There were also most delightful lakes fragrant with lotuses and blue water-lilies, filled with swans and kāraṇḍava ducks and graced by cakravāka birds.

sanskrit: ramyāś ca vividhās tatra puṣkariṇyo vanāvṛtāḥ taḍāgāni ca ramyāṇi bṛhanti ca mahānti ca
english: There were various charming lotus-ponds surrounded by groves, and beautiful tanks — both large and great.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ puṇyajanopetaṃ rāṣṭram āvasatāṃ mahat pāṇḍavānāṃ mahārāja śaśvat prītir avardhata
english: As those Pāṇḍavas dwelt in that great realm filled with virtuous people, O great king, their joy continuously increased.

sanskrit: tatra bhīṣmeṇa rājñā ca dharmapraṇayane kṛte pāṇḍavāḥ samapadyanta khāṇḍavaprasthavāsinaḥ
english: There, with the establishment of righteousness brought about by Bhīṣma and the king, the Pāṇḍavas became the settled inhabitants of Khāṇḍavaprastha.

sanskrit: pañcabhis tair maheṣvāsair indrakalpaiḥ samanvitam śuśubhe tat puraśreṣṭhaṃ nāgair bhogavatī yathā
english: Graced by those five mighty archers who were like Indra himself, that finest of cities shone just as Bhogavatī shines graced by the nāgas.

sanskrit: tān niveśya tato vīro rāmeṇa saha keśavaḥ yayau dvāravatīṃ rājan pāṇḍavānumate tadā
english: Having settled them there, that hero Keśava then departed for Dvāravatī together with Rāma, O king, with the consent of the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca evaṃ saṃprāpya rājyaṃ tad indraprasthe tapodhana ata ūrdhvaṃ mahātmānaḥ kim akurvanta pāṇḍavāḥ
english: Janamejaya said: O treasure of asceticism, having thus obtained that kingdom at Indraprastha, what thereafter did those great-souled Pāṇḍavas do?

sanskrit: sarva eva mahātmānaḥ pūrve mama pitāmahāḥ draupadī dharmapatnī ca kathaṃ tān anvavartata
english: All those great-souled men who were the forebears of my grandfather — how did Draupadī, the lawful wife, conduct herself toward them?

sanskrit: kathaṃ vā pañca kṛṣṇāyām ekasyāṃ te narādhipāḥ vartamānā mahābhāgā nābhidyanta parasparam
english: How was it that those five lords of men, all sharing the one Kṛṣṇā, though greatly blessed, did not become divided against one another?

sanskrit: śrotum icchāmy ahaṃ sarvaṃ vistareṇa tapodhana teṣāṃ ceṣṭitam anyonyaṃ yuktānāṃ kṛṣṇayā tayā
english: I wish to hear all of this in full detail, O treasure of asceticism — their conduct toward one another while they were united with that Kṛṣṇā.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca dhṛtarāṣṭrābhyanujñātāḥ kṛṣṇayā saha pāṇḍavāḥ remire puruṣavyāghrāḥ prāptarājyāḥ paraṃtapāḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Permitted by Dhṛtarāṣṭra, those tiger-men among men, the Pāṇḍavas, scorchers of foes, having obtained their kingdom, took their delight together with Kṛṣṇā.

sanskrit: prāpya rājyaṃ mahātejāḥ satyasaṃdho yudhiṣṭhiraḥ pālayām āsa dharmeṇa pṛthivīṃ bhrātṛbhiḥ saha
english: Having obtained the kingdom, the greatly resplendent Yudhiṣṭhira, true to his word, governed the earth righteously together with his brothers.

sanskrit: jitārayo mahāprājñāḥ satyadharmaparāyaṇāḥ mudaṃ paramikāṃ prāptās tatroṣuḥ pāṇḍunandanāḥ
english: Having vanquished their enemies, those greatly wise sons of Pāṇḍu, devoted to truth and righteousness, dwelt there having attained the highest joy.

sanskrit: kurvāṇāḥ paurakāryāṇi sarvāṇi puruṣarṣabhāḥ āsāṃ cakrur mahārheṣu pārthiveṣv āsaneṣu ca
english: Performing all duties toward the citizens, those bulls among men took their seats on magnificent royal thrones.

sanskrit: atha teṣūpaviṣṭeṣu sarveṣv eva mahātmasu nāradas tv atha devarṣir ājagāma yadṛcchayā āsanaṃ ruciraṃ tasmai pradadau svaṃ yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Then, while all those great-souled men were seated thus, the divine sage Nārada arrived of his own accord. Yudhiṣṭhira offered his own beautiful seat to him.

sanskrit: devarṣer upaviṣṭasya svayam arghyaṃ yathāvidhi prādād yudhiṣṭhiro dhīmān rājyaṃ cāsmai nyavedayat
english: Once the divine sage had taken his seat, the wise Yudhiṣṭhira himself offered him the arghya guest-gift according to due rite and presented his kingdom to him.

sanskrit: pratigṛhya tu tāṃ pūjām ṛṣiḥ prītamanābhavat āśīrbhir vardhayitvā tu tam uvācāsyatām iti
english: Having accepted that worship, the sage became glad at heart. After blessing him with benedictions he said to him: "Be seated."

sanskrit: niṣasādābhyanujñātas tato rājā yudhiṣṭhiraḥ preṣayām āsa kṛṣṇāyai bhagavantam upasthitam
english: Then King Yudhiṣṭhira, given leave, sat down, and sent word to Kṛṣṇā that the venerable one had arrived.

sanskrit: śrutvaiva draupadī cāpi śucir bhūtvā samāhitā jagāma tatra yatrāste nāradaḥ pāṇḍavaiḥ saha
english: On hearing this, Draupadī too, having purified herself and composed her mind, went to where Nārada was sitting with the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: tasyābhivādya caraṇau devarṣer dharmacāriṇī kṛtāñjaliḥ susaṃvītā sthitātha drupadātmajā
english: She who walks in the path of righteousness, the daughter of Drupada, bowed to the feet of the divine sage, stood with joined palms, well-veiled in her garment.

sanskrit: tasyāś cāpi sa dharmātmā satyavāg ṛṣisattamaḥ āśiṣo vividhāḥ procya rājaputryās tu nāradaḥ gamyatām iti hovāca bhagavāṃs tām aninditām
english: That righteous-souled, truth-speaking best of sages, Nārada, pronounced various blessings upon her, the princess, and the venerable one said to that blameless lady: "You may go."

sanskrit: gatāyām atha kṛṣṇāyāṃ yudhiṣṭhirapurogamān vivikte pāṇḍavān sarvān uvāca bhagavān ṛṣiḥ
english: Then, after Kṛṣṇā had gone, the venerable sage spoke privately to all the Pāṇḍavas with Yudhiṣṭhira at their head.

sanskrit: pāñcālī bhavatām ekā dharmapatnī yaśasvinī yathā vo nātra bhedaḥ syāt tathā nītir vidhīyatām
english: "The glorious Pāñcālī is the one lawful wife of you all. A rule must be established among you so that no dissension arises here.

sanskrit: sundopasundāv asurau bhrātarau sahitāv ubhau āstām avadhyāv anyeṣāṃ triṣu lokeṣu viśrutau
english: The two asuras Sunda and Upasunda were brothers who stood together — both invincible to all others, renowned in the three worlds.

sanskrit: ekarājyāv ekagṛhāv ekaśayyāsanāśanau tilottamāyās tau hetor anyonyam abhijaghnatuḥ
english: They shared one kingdom, one house, one bed, seat, and food — yet on account of Tilottamā those two killed each other.

sanskrit: rakṣyatāṃ sauhṛdaṃ tasmād anyonyapratibhāvikam yathā vo nātra bhedaḥ syāt tat kuruṣva yudhiṣṭhira
english: Therefore let a mutual friendship be safeguarded between you. Do what is necessary so that no division arises among you, O Yudhiṣṭhira."

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca sundopasundāv asurau kasya putrau mahāmune utpannaś ca kathaṃ bhedaḥ kathaṃ cānyonyam aghnatām
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: O great sage, whose sons were the asuras Sunda and Upasunda? How did the division arise among them, and how did they kill each other?

sanskrit: apsarā devakanyā vā kasya caiṣā tilottamā yasyāḥ kāmena saṃmattau jaghnatus tau parasparam
english: Was Tilottamā an apsarā or a daughter of the gods? Whose was she, maddened by desire for whom those two killed each other?

sanskrit: etat sarvaṃ yathāvṛttaṃ vistareṇa tapodhana śrotum icchāmahe vipra paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi naḥ
english: We wish to hear all of this exactly as it happened, and in full detail, O treasure of asceticism — for our curiosity is very great, O brahmin.

sanskrit: nārada uvāca śṛṇu me vistareṇemam itihāsaṃ purātanam bhrātṛbhīḥ sahitaḥ pārtha yathāvṛttaṃ yudhiṣṭhira
english: Nārada said: Hear from me in full this ancient tale exactly as it happened, O Pārtha Yudhiṣṭhira, together with your brothers.

sanskrit: mahāsurasyānvavāye hiraṇyakaśipoḥ purā nikumbho nāma daityendras tejasvī balavān abhūt
english: In the lineage of the great asura Hiraṇyakaśipu there was of old a lord of the daityas named Nikumbha, full of energy and great in strength.

sanskrit: tasya putrau mahāvīryau jātau bhīmaparākramau sahānyonyena bhuñjāte vinānyonyaṃ na gacchataḥ
english: His two sons were born of great valour and terrible might. They ate together, each with the other, and never went anywhere without the other.

sanskrit: anyonyasya priyakarāv anyonyasya priyaṃvadau ekaśīlasamācārau dvidhaivaikaṃ yathā kṛtau
english: Each was devoted to the pleasure of the other, each spoke words dear to the other; alike in character and conduct, they were as though one being divided into two.

sanskrit: tau vivṛddhau mahāvīryau kāryeṣv apy ekaniścayau trailokyavijayārthāya samāsthāyaikaniścayam
english: Those two, grown great and mighty, with a single resolve even in their undertakings, took a single firm resolution: to conquer the three worlds.

sanskrit: kṛtvā dīkṣāṃ gatau vindhyaṃ tatrograṃ tepatus tapaḥ tau tu dīrgheṇa kālena tapoyuktau babhūvatuḥ
english: Taking the rite of consecration, they went to the Vindhya mountain and there performed fierce austerities. After a long time they became fully absorbed in tapas.

sanskrit: kṣutpipāsāpariśrāntau jaṭāvalkaladhāriṇau malopacitasarvāṅgau vāyubhakṣau babhūvatuḥ
english: Exhausted by hunger and thirst, wearing matted locks and bark-cloth garments, with all their limbs encrusted with dirt, they became subsisting on air alone.

sanskrit: ātmamāṃsāni juhvantau pādāṅguṣṭhāgradhiṣṭhitau ūrdhvabāhū cānimiṣau dīrghakālaṃ dhṛtavratau
english: Offering oblations of their own flesh, standing balanced on the tips of their big toes, arms raised upward, eyes unblinking, they maintained their vow for a long time.

sanskrit: tayos tapaḥprabhāveṇa dīrghakālaṃ pratāpitaḥ dhūmaṃ pramumuce vindhyas tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: By the power of their austerities, the Vindhya mountain, scorched for a long time, began to emit smoke — and that seemed like a wonder.

sanskrit: tato devābhavan bhītā ugraṃ dṛṣṭvā tayos tapaḥ tapovighātārtham atho devā vighnāni cakrire
english: Then the gods became frightened on seeing their fierce austerities, and the gods created obstacles for the purpose of disrupting their tapas.

sanskrit: ratnaiḥ pralobhayām āsuḥ strībhiś cobhau punaḥ punaḥ na ca tau cakratur bhaṅgaṃ vratasya sumahāvratau
english: They repeatedly tempted the two with jewels and women, again and again — but those two, so mighty in their vow, did not break their vow.

sanskrit: atha māyāṃ punar devās tayoś cakrur mahātmanoḥ bhaginyo mātaro bhāryās tayoḥ parijanas tathā
english: Then the gods devised another illusion for those two great-souled ones — their sisters, mothers, wives, and their retinue of attendants,

sanskrit: paripātyamānā vitrastāḥ śūlahastena rakṣasā srastābharaṇakeśāntā ekāntabhraṣṭavāsasaḥ
english: — being chased in terror by a demon holding a trident, their ornaments and hair dishevelled, their garments slipping from their bodies,

sanskrit: abhidhāvya tataḥ sarvās tau trāhīti vicukruśuḥ na ca tau cakratur bhaṅgaṃ vratasya sumahāvratau
english: — all running toward them crying "Save us! Save us!" Yet those two, so mighty in their vow, did not break their vow.

sanskrit: yadā kṣobhaṃ nopayāti nārtim anyataras tayoḥ tataḥ striyas tā bhūtaṃ ca sarvam antaradhīyata
english: When neither of the two was moved to agitation or distress, those women and all that apparition vanished away entirely.

sanskrit: tataḥ pitāmahaḥ sākṣād abhigamya mahāsurau vareṇa chandayām āsa sarvalokapitāmahaḥ
english: Then the Grandfather himself, Brahmā the grandfather of all worlds, approached those two great asuras in person and offered them a boon of their choosing.

sanskrit: tataḥ sundopasundau tau bhrātarau dṛḍhavikramau dṛṣṭvā pitāmahaṃ devaṃ tasthatuḥ prāñjalī tadā
english: Then those two brothers, Sunda and Upasunda, firm in their valour, on seeing the divine Grandfather, stood with joined palms.

sanskrit: ūcatuś ca prabhuṃ devaṃ tatas tau sahitau tadā āvayos tapasānena yadi prītaḥ pitāmahaḥ
english: And then those two spoke together to the divine Lord: "If the Grandfather is pleased with this our austerity —

sanskrit: māyāvidāv astravidau balinau kāmarūpiṇau ubhāv apy amarau syāvaḥ prasanno yadi nau prabhuḥ
english: — may we both be masters of illusion, masters of weapons, mighty, able to assume any form at will, and both immortal — if the Lord is pleased with us."

sanskrit: pitāmaha uvāca ṛte 'maratvam anyad vāṃ sarvam uktaṃ bhaviṣyati anyad vṛṇītāṃ mṛtyoś ca vidhānam amaraiḥ samam
english: The Grandfather said: Except for immortality, everything else you have asked shall be granted. Choose instead a manner of death equal to that of the immortals.

sanskrit: kariṣyāvedam iti yan mahad abhyutthitaṃ tapaḥ yuvayor hetunānena nāmaratvaṃ vidhīyate
english: "The great austerity you two have undertaken with the aim of doing this — on account of that very purpose, immortality cannot be ordained.

sanskrit: trailokyavijayārthāya bhavadbhyām āsthitaṃ tapaḥ hetunānena daityendrau na vāṃ kāmaṃ karomy aham
english: "The austerity has been undertaken by you two for the purpose of conquering the three worlds — on this account, O lords of the daityas, I cannot grant you that wish."

sanskrit: sundopasundāv ūcatuḥ triṣu lokeṣu yad bhūtaṃ kiṃ cit sthāvarajaṅgamam sarvasmān nau bhayaṃ na syād ṛte 'nyonyaṃ pitāmaha
english: Sunda and Upasunda said: May we have no fear from anything whatsoever — whether movable or immovable — in the three worlds, except from each other, O Grandfather.

sanskrit: pitāmaha uvāca yat prārthitaṃ yathoktaṃ ca kāmam etad dadāni vām mṛtyor vidhānam etac ca yathāvad vāṃ bhaviṣyati
english: The Grandfather said: This boon that you have asked for and stated — this wish I grant you both. And this manner of death shall indeed come to pass for you as ordained.

sanskrit: nārada uvāca tataḥ pitāmaho dattvā varam etat tadā tayoḥ nivartya tapasas tau ca brahmalokaṃ jagāma ha
english: Nārada said: Then the Grandfather, having granted them that boon and caused them to cease their austerities, departed to the world of Brahmā.

sanskrit: labdhvā varāṇi sarvāṇi daityendrāv api tāv ubhau avadhyau sarvalokasya svam eva bhavanaṃ gatau
english: Having obtained all the boons, those two lords of the daityas, now invincible to all the worlds, returned to their own dwelling.

sanskrit: tau tu labdhavarau dṛṣṭvā kṛtakāmau mahāsurau sarvaḥ suhṛjjanas tābhyāṃ pramodam upajagmivān
english: Seeing those two great asuras who had obtained their boons and fulfilled their desire, all their circle of friends and kinsmen rejoiced greatly on their account.

sanskrit: tatas tau tu jaṭā hitvā maulinau saṃbabhūvatuḥ mahārhābharaṇopetau virajombaradhāriṇau
english: Then those two, discarding their matted locks, became adorned with crowns, decked with the most precious ornaments, and wearing spotless garments.

sanskrit: akālakaumudīṃ caiva cakratuḥ sārvakāmikīm daityendrau paramaprītau tayoś caiva suhṛjjanaḥ
english: Those two lords of the daityas, supremely delighted, held an out-of-season moonlit festival fulfilling every desire, as did their circle of friends.

sanskrit: bhakṣyatāṃ bhujyatāṃ nityaṃ ramyatāṃ gīyatām iti pīyatāṃ dīyatāṃ ceti vāca āsan gṛhe gṛhe
english: "Eat! Feast! Make merry! Sing! Drink! Give!" — such were the cries that rang out in house after house.

sanskrit: tatra tatra mahāpānair utkṛṣṭatalanāditaiḥ hṛṣṭaṃ pramuditaṃ sarvaṃ daityānām abhavat puram
english: Here and there, with great drinking bouts resounding with the sound of clapping and cymbals, the entire city of the daityas became full of gladness and merriment.

sanskrit: tais tair vihārair bahubhir daityānāṃ kāmarūpiṇām samāḥ saṃkrīḍatāṃ teṣām ahar ekam ivābhavat
english: Through those many and various diversions of the daityas who could assume any form at will, years passed in play for them as though they were but a single day.

sanskrit: nārada uvāca utsave vṛttamātre tu trailokyākāṅkṣiṇāv ubhau mantrayitvā tataḥ senāṃ tāv ājñāpayatāṃ tadā
english: Nārada said: But as soon as the festival was over, those two who longed to conquer the three worlds took counsel and then gave orders to the army.

sanskrit: suhṛdbhir abhyanujñātau daityavṛddhaiś ca mantribhiḥ kṛtvā prāsthānikaṃ rātrau maghāsu yayatus tadā
english: Sent off with the blessings of their friends and the elder daitya counsellors, having performed the departure rites, they set out at night under the Maghā constellation.

sanskrit: gadāpaṭṭiśadhāriṇyā śūlamudgarahastayā prasthitau sahadharmiṇyā mahatyā daityasenayā
english: They set out accompanied by a great daitya army, bearing maces and paṭṭiśa blades, armed with tridents and hammers in hand.

sanskrit: maṅgalaiḥ stutibhiś cāpi vijayapratisaṃhitaiḥ cāraṇaiḥ stūyamānau tu jagmatuḥ parayā mudā
english: Praised by bards with auspicious hymns and victory songs, those two marched forth with the greatest joy.

sanskrit: tāv antarikṣam utpatya daityau kāmagamāv ubhau devānām eva bhavanaṃ jagmatur yuddhadurmadau
english: Those two daityas, both able to go wherever they willed, rose up into the sky and made their way toward the very dwelling of the gods, intoxicated with the desire for battle.

sanskrit: tayor āgamanaṃ jñātvā varadānaṃ ca tat prabhoḥ hitvā triviṣṭapaṃ jagmur brahmalokaṃ tataḥ surāḥ
english: Learning of their coming and of that boon granted by the Lord, the gods thereupon abandoned heaven and departed to the world of Brahmā.

sanskrit: tāv indralokaṃ nirjitya yakṣarakṣogaṇāṃs tathā khecarāṇy api bhūtāni jigyatus tīvravikramau
english: Those two, fierce in their valour, conquered the realm of Indra and likewise the hosts of yakṣas and rākṣasas, and vanquished even the sky-moving beings.
